messages:
Raj Patel: Quick heads-up — Acme legal asked for a DPA + SCC language they can drop into procurement. They also want a clear DSAR/deletion SLA: how quickly we can remove PII from active storage, logs, and backups. POC with their infra team next Wed. Need legal + security signoff by EOW.
Amanda Chen: Got it. Do they want EU-only controls or global?
Raj Patel: EU-first. They want explicit SCCs reference + clause about data residency fallback if SCCs are updated.
Oliver Ruiz: For backups: standard practice is we can guarantee deletion from active stores within 30 days, but backups are tricky — we can commit to not restoring PII from backups beyond X retention and to scrub on restore. Is that acceptable?
Hannah Li: Can we offer a tiered SLA: 30 days active delete, 90 days for logs (redacted), and 180 days for cold backups with documented restore-only process? They ask for concrete numbers.
Marta K (security): We cannot promise deletion from immutable backups within 30 days unless we change retention architecture. Suggest language:
```
We will delete Customer Personal Data from active systems within 30 days of a valid deletion request. Backups are retained for disaster recovery; we will not use backups for any purpose other than restoration and will implement restore-time redaction/ purge procedures. Restores that might reintroduce Personal Data will be remediated within 14 days of detection.
```
Marta K (security): Also: include the standard SCC reference block and a note about subprocessors and notification timelines (30 days).
sales-bot: Checklist created: [DPA draft] [SCC clause] [POC dataflow diagram] [Deletion playbook]. Assigned: @Amanda, @Marta.
Amanda Chen: I’ll draft DPA copy with the 30/90/180 tier and push to drive. Will include example SCC text and a short runbook for the POC.
Oliver Ruiz: For the POC, they want to run DSAR and deletion tests against a sandbox. We should provide a scoped dataset (anonymized) + instructions. Can infra spin up a time-limited sandbox? @Hannah Li
Hannah Li: Yes, we can. Will provision ephemeral VPC + logs disabled by default. Need list of endpoints and sample data fields.
Raj Patel: Acme also asked about CAIQ/SIG answers. They want to know if any control gaps exist for data subject rights. Can security produce a one-page summary?
Marta K (security): I’ll produce a CAIQ-highlighted notes doc that maps our controls to DSAR/DPA requirements (turnaround times, authn, audit). Expect a draft by tomorrow afternoon.
Amanda Chen: For procurement, they sometimes want specific contract language. I’ll prepare two versions: one with the standard Redwood clause and one with a customer-specific addendum (if needed).
Raj Patel: Perfect. If we can get Marta + Amanda signoff by EOW, I’ll share with Acme before the POC. Also confirm pricing note — they asked whether deletion costs are included or billable.
Oliver Ruiz: Deletion ops are included for regular requests. If they request forensic/restore work outside standard deletes -> billable. Put that in the DPA exceptions.
Marta K (security): Also add a mitigation sentence around SCC updates: we will adopt new SCCs within 60 days or provide an alternative mechanism.
Amanda Chen: Draft pushed: https://drive.redwood/acme-dpa-draft (internal link). Feedback welcome.
Raj Patel: Thanks team — I’ll update the Acme buyer after Marta's CAIQ summary. 
Hannah Li: FYI I added the sandbox creation ticket to eng backlog #8942. ETA Tue morning.
Oliver Ruiz: One more ask from Acme — they want a template deletion verification report after tests. Can we provide a signed PDF with logs/artefacts (redacted)?
Marta K (security): Yes — we can provide an audit report template. It will contain the test steps, results, and a signed attestation.
Raj Patel: Great. Closing loop: deliverables by EOW: DPA draft, CAIQ highlight, deletion playbook, sandbox ready. I’ll follow up in a quick call tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Amanda Chen: Sounds good.
sales-bot: Reminder scheduled: Meeting with Acme POC — Wed 10:00 AM (UTC).
